- When sentiment is low (≤0.18) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), reduce next period’s forecast by 3–5% to correct for momentum overcorrection.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.36) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 2–5% to capture bullish momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (especially after 10–15 days), apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% from forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is flat or negative and forecast is high, apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% for each day after the last sentiment peak.
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 7-day low unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.44) — otherwise, adjust upward to avoid underestimating rebound.
